en_title: Medication Can Help Open the Door, but Training and Habit Change Keep the Results
en_excerpt: GLP-1 medication can be life-changing when properly indicated — but without strength training and enough protein, part of the weight lost can be muscle.
en_meta_description: A personal trainer on Ozempic, Mounjaro and GLP-1: why strength training, protein and habits decide whether results last.
en_content:
Text: Ana Paula, Personal Trainer

https://www.instagram.com/fitandstrongwithana/

Medication can help open the door, but it is training and habit change that will keep the results. First I want to say that I do not believe that Mounjaro/ Ozempic or, in general, GLP-1 class medication is only a “shortcut”, but I also do not believe it should be used by just anyone who thinks they need to lose weight!

For some people, these medications can change lives, especially for those who have struggled for years with obesity, binge eating or insulin resistance.

And science has already shown that the benefits go beyond weight loss. The SELECT study, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, showed that semaglutide (Ozempic/Wegovy) significantly reduced the risk of cardiovascular events in people with obesity or excess weight, even without diabetes.

But I also need to say this: it is not a magic solution.

I see many people who believe that the pen does all the work. The reality is that these medications can help a great deal with weight loss, BUT without strength training, enough protein and habit change, there is a risk of losing muscle mass as well, not only fat.

And this is important: recent studies on body composition in GLP-1 users show that part of the weight loss may come from lean body mass (lean mass), which makes strength training even more important during the process.

If you are using Ozempic or Mounjaro, and I hope in a medically supervised way, strength training becomes even more important.

The goal should not be only “weighing less”. The goal should be:

✔ lose fat

✔ keep (or gain) muscle mass

✔ improve metabolic health

✔ create sustainable habits

Another important point: studies show that when the medication is combined with physical exercise, the results tend to be more sustainable and less likely to lead to weight regain.

The truth is this:

Medication can help open the door, but training and habit change will help to keep the results.

As a personal trainer, my opinion is simple: I do not judge anyone who uses it, but I always reinforce the importance of using it with medical follow-up and truly in necessary cases.

Now imagine that you suddenly decide you want to use it to lose 2kg because you think you need to, and to stop eating compulsively, or to silence the “food noise ” as we call it in English?

I do not believe that this is the best solution, and when should you stop using the medication? I believe that the best solution and the most efficient way to lose weight in this case and keep it off would be to treat the reasons why you eat compulsively and the reasons behind the “food noise ”

To finish, my view is this: these tools can be extremely useful when well indicated, but what really sustains results in the long term continues to be the basics done well — consistency, training, food and behaviour change.

References:

1. Rubino D. et al. Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity (SURMOUNT-1). New England Journal of Medicine. 2. Lincoff AM. et al. Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes (SELECT). New England Journal of Medicine. 3. Recent reviews on body composition and lean mass loss with GLP-1 therapies (lean mass preservation). PubMed Central. 4. Studies on weight-loss maintenance with exercise + GLP-1. The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology.
